correctness.rationale: With opposite fixed endpoints, each of the two paths has a single-domain-wall recurrent class and a finite reversible interface birth–death walk. Two paths are dynamically independent; the total-count variance is W_a(q)+W_(6-a)(q), where W_L(q)=q/(1-q)^2-L^2*q^L/(1-q^L)^2 and W_L(1)=(L^2-1)/12. Exact rational subtraction gives the two phase polynomials P(z),Q(z), z=q+1/q. Descartes sign-change analysis of P(2+t) and Q(2+t), plus their endpoint signs, proves a unique root above 2 for each, ordered by rational evaluation at z=27/10. The signs prove all three strict regimes and exactly the two boundary ties. A standalone independently constructed 16-state generator was solved at nine exact rational cases; this is corroboration, not a substitute for the continuum proof. All stated endpoint and reversal cases were checked.

value.rationale: Stationary opinion-count variance is an established social-network fluctuation target (Yildiz et al. 2011). The six-agent cycle is the minimal geometric setting with a third, strictly intermediate separation, and it exhibits a nonempty exact parameter phase where this intermediate separation is uniquely optimal. The algebraic boundaries exhibit a qualitative reversal of optimal committed-agent spacing under directional asymmetry, not just an isolated small numerical gain or recomputation of a known table. It provides a sharp finite counterexample to endpoint-only spacing heuristics and a benchmark for asymmetrically weighted stubborn-agent networks. The finding does not claim empirical policy validity or general-graph optimality.
